raw_response:
I will start from what has worked for me around Quzhou County and adjust a little for cost and water. I have 50 mu and a well, so I am not farming blind on rainfall, and that lets me push fertilizer a bit more safely. For stevia, I will put more land there because that is the crop system I am already centered on, and I will feed it a bit heavier on nitrogen and potassium so the leaves stay strong and I can cut for good output. For cotton, I will keep a smaller block, use improved seed, and not let fertilizer get too low because once cotton falls behind early, it is hard to bring back. I usually look at what fields around me did well last year, and the good fields were not the ones saving too hard on base fertilizer. With 50 mu, I also have to think about labor and spray cost, so I will plough once before the season, use water from the well on the key growth stages, and keep pesticide sprays on a fixed count instead of waiting until damage gets too heavy.
